methodological_rigor.justification: The study is a small single-center case-control/cross-sectional serum biomarker study (90 PCa, 30 BPH, 60 controls) with no independent validation cohort, no pre-specified sample size or power calculation, and no blinding of RT-qPCR operators reported. The diagnostic cut-off for the ROC analysis appears to be derived and evaluated on the same cohort without train/test splitting, risking overfitting, and the Cox multivariate analysis with 90 PCa patients is likely underpowered given multiple co-entered predictors (TNM, Gleason, bone metastasis, circRNA). Mechanistic claims rest entirely on in silico target prediction and two small public GEO datasets (one with n=5 pairs, another with a single tumor/normal pair), with no functional perturbation. Statistical handling is basic (t-test/ANOVA/chi-square/Cox) with no multiplicity correction across multiple clinicopathological associations and no effect sizes beyond HRs for Cox.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a small single-center case-control style biomarker study with exploratory prognostic analysis, mapping to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case-control). Clinical relevance is modest: an AUC of 0.773 with 74.4% sensitivity and 88.3% specificity is not superior to or clearly additive with PSA, and no head-to-head comparison or combined PSA+circRNA model is presented. The circRNA failed to remain an independent prognostic factor on multivariate Cox, further limiting translational impact. The authors appropriately note that validation in larger independent cohorts is required before clinical application.

reporting_quality.justification: As a tumor biomarker study, REMARK is the appropriate standard; most core items (patient selection, assay description, primers, clinicopathological associations, univariate/multivariate Cox) are reported, but several REMARK elements are incomplete: no flow diagram of patient inclusion, no explicit handling of missing data, no blinding statement, no pre-specified cut-off derivation, and limited follow-up description. Ethics approval and informed consent are stated. Data availability is weak: public GEO dataset IDs are cited (GSE113153, GSE155792, GSE119338, GSE14857), but no statement about sharing of the patient-level serum qPCR data or analysis code is present, and one database URL is redacted.

novelty_literature.justification: The work is a meaningful but incremental extension: hsa_circ_0006168 has already been characterized as oncogenic in ESCC (Shi et al., 2019) and glioblastoma (Wang et al., 2021), and the manuscript's contribution is to test its serum expression in PCa and link it to Gleason score. The claim of being the first serum characterization in PCa and the speculative AR/miR-205 axis add some originality, but the mechanism is entirely in silico and many PCa circRNA biomarker papers (circHIPK3, circ0005276, circGNG4, circSOBP) are cited for context. This represents a single directional extension of prior work rather than a novel concept or method.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable and follows a standard IMRaD structure, with the results logically organized (bioinformatics, serum validation, ROC, clinicopathological, Cox, mechanism). There are minor grammatical slips (e.g., 'an previous study', 'Inclusion criteria were'), some redundancy between Results and Discussion, and figures/tables are referenced but described only at summary level. Key numeric results (AUC, 95% CI, sensitivity, specificity, C-index) are clearly reported inline, and limitations are acknowledged, though a cleaner Methods flow (e.g., follow-up duration, censoring) would help.

key_strengths: Clear clinical question addressing the well-documented specificity limitations of PSA with a non-invasive serum biomarker candidate
Assay quality evidence provided: linearity R2=0.9943, reproducibility, stability across freeze-thaw and ambient temperature
Quantitative diagnostic metrics reported with 95% CI (AUC 0.773, CI 0.698-0.847; sensitivity 74.4%; specificity 88.3%)
Honest acknowledgment of limitations (single-center, small sample, mechanism is in silico only, loss of independence on multivariate Cox)
key_concerns: Small single-center cohort (90 PCa) with no independent validation set; ROC cut-off appears derived and evaluated on the same data, risking overfitting
No comparison or combined model against PSA, undermining the claimed advance over the standard biomarker
Mechanistic claims (p53 pathway, miR-205 sponging, AR axis) rest entirely on in silico prediction and tiny public GEO datasets (n=5 pairs; single tumor/normal pair) with no functional validation
hsa_circ_0006168 lost prognostic independence in multivariate Cox, limiting the prognostic claim highlighted in the abstract
No multiplicity correction across multiple clinicopathological association tests; no power calculation; no patient-level data or analysis code sharing statement
Partial REMARK adherence: missing flow diagram, blinding, missing-data handling, and explicit cut-off derivation procedure
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a competently executed but small, single-center, exploratory biomarker study with modest diagnostic performance, no independent validation, and entirely in silico mechanism. Methodological rigor and clinical relevance limitations place it at tier 4 (low-JIF oncology journal) with major revisions needed to address validation, PSA comparison, and REMARK gaps.
